newsitem.title: FINLAND: KESKO SEES NO CANCELLATION OF TUKO DEAL.
newsitem.headline: KESKO SEES NO CANCELLATION OF TUKO DEAL.

text.p: Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko Oy CEO Eero Kinnunen said on Wednesday he does not expect the European Commission to cancel Kesko's acquisition of Tuko although the deal may be against EU merger rules.
"There is no hints whatsoever to that direction," Kinnunen told Reuters by telephone, when asked whether he thought the commission might reject the deal.
The EU commision on September 17 released a statement saying the Kesko-Tuko deal may be against EU merger legislation.
But Kinnunen said Kesko may have to change its organisation somehow to get the commission's approval.
"Obviously there will be some changes. I have a feeling that these will concern the relation between us and the shopkeepers," he said.

Kinnunen said the commission feared that Kesko could get a dominating market position as they regard Kesko as a chain store. Kesko regards itself as a wholesaler and a supplier catering to independent shopkeepers in the K-group.
"They look at us as if we were a chain store, but this is a group of independent, voluntary shopkeepers," he said.
Kesko has three weeks to supply the commission with more information, and the commission will take its final decision by November 27, Kinnunen said.
Kesko bought a majority in rival wholesaler Tuko late in May.
